paper.title_en: Interference-caged quantum many-body scars: Local ETH-violation witnesses and deformation stability
paper.abstract_en: Many-body interference can render an exact eigenstate locally nonthermal by canceling a microscopic process active in thermal states. We formulate the Fock-space analogue of compact flat-band localization as \emph{interference caging}: escape amplitudes cancel exactly across the active boundary of a set of product configurations. We give sufficient conditions to reduce this configuration-dependent cancellation to a fixed real-space region, yielding a bounded local caging operator. Its positive square vanishes on the caged eigenstate and witnesses violation of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) if its microcanonical expectation for the same Hamiltonian and energy density remains bounded away from zero in the thermodynamic limit. We call these states \emph{interference-caged quantum many-body scars} (ICQMBS) when they form a vanishing fraction of a symmetry-resolved bulk energy window whose typical eigenstates are locally thermal for every bounded local observable. The mechanism is independent of quasiparticle, algebraic, or symmetry-based constructions and compatible with Hilbert-space fragmentation. Our chiral-shell search constructs exact caged eigenstates from allowed transitions without a preselected wavefunction, target subspace, or ladder operator. We identify local ETH-violation witnesses, test their deformation stability, and demonstrate thermal contrast in two systems. In the spin-1 XY chain, we recover the known scar tower, also describable through quasiparticles and projector embedding, and prove ICQMBS throughout an open interval of compatible exchange couplings in the thermodynamic limit. In the square-lattice quantum dimer model, we construct exact caged eigenstates and local operators from plaquette flips on fixed-width strips under a checkerboard phase deformation; finite-size microcanonical comparisons support thermal contrast.
